title: SLO-horizon interruptor with KV tenancy decay and progressive preemption
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Problem: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization but introduces complex preemption trade-offs when GPU memory (KV cache + model state) becomes constrained. Current hard-preempt approaches either violate tenant latency SLOs or evict cache too aggressively, causing quality regressions and thundering re-warm. Goal: design and implement an SLO-aware interruptor that (1) minimizes SLO breaches, (2) reduces harmful KV thrash, and (3) reclaims memory in a graded, predictable way.
updates: 2025-11-07: Spike complete — benchmarked baseline continuous batching with 95th P99 latency SLO buffer per tenant; identified worst-case KV pressure patterns from bursty multi-tenant workloads (synthetic replay).

2025-11-09: Design proposal drafted: introduce an SLO-horizon score (slack/time-to-SLO-violation) + tenancy decay metric (age-weighted access frequency) to drive a three-stage progressive preemption: 1) soft-shed (reduce batch admission rate for offending tenant), 2) tuned KV soft-evict (evict cold KV segments with decay score), 3) slice-steal (reclaim micro-slices from long-running low-priority queues).

2025-11-10: Prototype implemented in the local preemptor shim; added horizon estimator that predicts eviction impact on 95th latency using recent per-tenant latency slope. Initial sim shows ~65% reduction in SLO violations vs current instantaneous preempt policy at 10% throughput loss for low-priority tenants.

2025-11-11: Engineering review (runtime team) feedback: need explicit anti-thrashing guards (minimum re-warm interval per tenant) and backpressure-aware admission tokens to avoid oscillation under correlated bursts.
2025-11-12: PM feedback (Aisha Malik): require clear rollout gating, metrics, and a canary that can be toggled per-customer (Dedicated/Private) — added per-tenant flag and telemetry plan.

2025-11-13: Created design doc and linked prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284 (WIP). Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SLO-Horizon-Interruptor (draft).

2025-11-14: Performance run against multi-tenant production trace (7 days): progressive preemption kept P99 within SLO for 93% of tenants vs 78% baseline; KV eviction volume reduced by 42% (measured bytes evicted), but mean throughput for P3 tenants decreased ~12%. Decision: proceed to canary with monitoring and automatic rollback if customer P99 increase > 10%.

Next steps: add anti-thrashing timers, instrument per-tenant re-warm cost, implement admission token bucket in the router, document rollout playbook and SLOs for canary; plan 2-week canary on a dedicated pool.

Follow-ups: link to telemetry dashboards (TODO), create infra job to sweep stale KV segments with tenancy decay policy, and coordinate with Console team for per-route visualization of preemption events.
acceptance_criteria: Canary toggle available and documented; can be enabled per pool/customer via feature flag.
Telemetries: per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency, preemption events, KV-evict bytes, re-warm misses instrumented and show expected delta in the dashboard.

Controlled experiment: in a representative multi-tenant workload, the SLO-horizon interruptor reduces P99 SLO breaches by >= 30% compared to baseline with no more than 15% throughput loss for P2/P3 tenants.
Anti-thrashing: minimum re-warm interval enforced and verified (no tenant re-warm cycles shorter than configured window in 24h run).
Automated rollback: runbook and automation to roll back the interruptor for a pool if customer P99 increases > 10% within 1h of enabling.
Code: unit + integration tests for horizon estimator, tenancy decay scoring, and staged-preemption transitions merged behind feature flag (PR linked in updates).
